title: Strain-Tunable High-$T_c$ Superconductivity in Layered R3m B$_2$CN
authors: Durjay Dhali, Arafat Rahman, Tareq Mahmud, Alamgir Kabir
abstract: Using DFPT and Wannier-interpolated matrix elements in EPW, we find that isotropic tensile strain of 0--6\% narrows the B:2$p$/C:2$p$ bands at the Fermi level while softening the phonon branches most strongly coupled to them, driving the coupling constant $λ$ from 0.967 to 2.620. All four strained configurations remain mechanically and dynamically stable, satisfying the Born--Huang criteria with no imaginary phonon modes at any strain level. The fully anisotropic Migdal--Eliashberg equations give a $T_c$ that rises monotonically from 53.5~K to 84.5~K across the strain series, crossing the liquid-nitrogen boiling point at 6\% strain. The SISSO-based machine-learning model in EPW agrees with the anisotropic Migdal--Eliashberg $T_c$ values to within 10~K across the strain series.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that applying tensile strain to $	ext{R}3m 	ext{B}_2	ext{CN}$ enhances its superconducting properties. By calculating changes in electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$) using DFT and the Migdal-Eliashberg theory, the authors show that strain drives $T_c$ above the liquid-nitrogen boiling point. This work highlights strain engineering as a powerful tool for realizing high-temperature superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates how applying isotropic tensile strain tunes the superconducting properties and critical temperature ($T_c$) in the layered $	ext{R}3m 	ext{B}_2	ext{CN}$ material.
main_result: Tensile strain significantly enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$) from 0.967 to 2.620, leading to a monotonic increase in $T_c$ from 53.5 K to 84.5 K, crossing the liquid-nitrogen boiling point at 6% strain.
method: The research employs Density Functional Theory (DFT) combined with advanced calculations like DFPT for lattice dynamics and the anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg equations for superconductivity.
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered $	ext{R}3m 	ext{B}_2	ext{CN}$ crystal, analyzed across tensile strains from 0% to 6%. The theory models superconductivity via electron-phonon coupling, which is sensitive to strain-induced changes in electronic structure and phonon softening.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$), phonon softening, and the superconducting gap ($\Delta_0/k_B T_c$).
important_parameters: Strain levels (0% to 6%), $\lambda$ (0.967 to 2.620), and the Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the material remains mechanically and dynamically stable across the entire strain range, and it utilizes the anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, electronic band structures and DOS under strain, and phonon dispersions, while tables summarize elastic constants and superconducting gap values.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the mechanical stability (Born-Huang criteria) first, followed by electronic structure changes (band narrowing, $N(E_F)$ increase), and finally calculates the resulting superconducting properties using the anisotropic Eliashberg equations.
why_interesting: The direct link established between mechanical strain, lattice dynamics (phonon softening), and the enhancement of electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$) to boost $T_c$ is a key concept in understanding emergent quantum phenomena in solid-state materials.
